title: Red Side Up
statement: A hat holds three cards: one red on both sides, one white on both sides, and one red on one side and white on the other. You draw a card at random and look at one random side. It is red. What is the probability the other side is also red?
insight: Condition on faces, not cards: there are three equally likely red faces and two of them belong to the red-red card.
redHerring: Saying 1/2 because 'it is either the red-red card or the mixed card'. Those two cards are not equally likely given what you saw.
hints: What are the equally likely outcomes of drawing a card and showing a side?
There are 6 equally likely (card, side) outcomes. How many show red?
Of the red faces, how many have red on the back?
solution: Each of the 6 faces is equally likely to be the one shown. Three are red: two on the red-red card, one on the mixed card. Given red is showing, the other side is red in 2 of these 3 cases: $\tfrac23$.
